results.summary: Under 42 CFR 430.20, a State plan amendment generally cannot be effective earlier than the first day of the calendar quarter in which an approvable amendment is submitted to CMS, and these rules exist to establish when federal financial participation (FFP) is available. Amendments that add services, raise payment amounts, or add eligibility groups follow the same rule as new plans (430.20(a)); amendments changing payment methods and standards follow 42 CFR 447.256. The one explicit flexibility is for "other" plan amendments, where the effective date may be a date requested by the state if CMS approves it. So a pre-submission (retroactive) effective date is not available under the standard rules, but is possible only in that discretionary "other amendment" category.

arguments.summary: Yes — federal Medicaid drug use review (DUR) rules require the State plan to provide for review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered, using point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review with predetermined standards. The screening must identify seven specified types of potential drug therapy problems, from therapeutic duplication through clinical abuse/misuse. The obligation is framed as a State plan requirement with detailed instructions that pharmacies, in turn, must pass to their pharmacists, and narrow exceptions apply for certain nursing facility, hospital, and HMO dispensing.

findings.statement: Except for the §456.703(b)/(c) exceptions, the State plan must provide for review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered to a beneficiary, with applicable State law establishing counseling standards; the State must give pharmacies detailed information on what they must do to comply with prospective DUR (guidelines on counseling, profiling, documentation), and pharmacies must relay that to their pharmacists [42-CFR-456.705(a)].

The State plan must provide for point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered, and that review must include screening for specified types of potential drug therapy problems [42-CFR-456.705(b)].

Required screening types (1)-(2): therapeutic duplication (two or more drugs from the same therapeutic class where the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or extra cost without added benefit) and drug-disease contraindication [42-CFR-456.705(b)] [42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Required screening types (3)-(6): adverse drug-drug interaction (clinically significant adverse effect from using two or more drugs together), incorrect drug dosage (outside the daily dosage in predetermined standards; dosage = strength × quantity dispensed ÷ day's supply), incorrect duration of drug treatment (exceeds or falls short of standards), and drug-allergy interactions [42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Required screening type (7): clinical abuse/misuse, i.e., situations falling under the definitions of abuse, gross overuse, overutilization and related terms; retrospective DUR separately monitors over/underutilization and the same problem types [42-CFR-456.705(b)-2, 42-CFR-456.709(b)].

Exceptions: prospective DUR is not required for drugs dispensed to residents of nursing facilities in compliance with part 483 drug regimen review procedures [42-CFR-456.703(b)], nor for covered outpatient drugs dispensed by hospitals using formulary systems and billed at no more than purchasing cost, or dispensed by HMOs [42-CFR-456.703(c)].
